title: macOS bun test wedge: bun runtime bisect with a symbolicated sample, and the return to macos-latest (macos-15 pin landed in #700)
description:
The macOS leg of main push CI (`lint · typecheck · test (macos-latest)`, bun 1.3.14 via .bun-version, run-hang-guarded.mjs --silence-seconds 120) went from green on every main push read back to 38025163174 (last green 619f02cf, run 39889231736, 2026-10-23, 7-10 min, no SILENT annotation) to RED on both main pushes after tonight's promotions: ca31e9ae (run 41165975631, plus its --failed rerun, job 124438724067) and 2cca01dd (run 41169408076, job 124443904878). Every attempt (6 passes over 3 job runs) went silent for 120s, was sampled and killed, and the single hang-retry also hung: "attempt 2 ALSO failed after the hang retry ... (LCLI-760)".

EVIDENCE (read by log, 2026-10-31). Hang points differ every pass, so it is NOT one hung test: test/check.test.ts after two different tests, test/release-workflow.test.ts after "every npm publish in release.yml stages under release-candidate, and nothing writes latest", test/agent-context-constitution.test.ts after the AC2 dedupe tests. The process sample shows bun's main thread in kevent64 with ~96% CPU and a defunct child (symbols stripped). No assertion failure anywhere. ubuntu, windows and docker e2e legs of the same runs are green. macOS never runs on a PR (ci.yml: PR matrix is ubuntu+windows), so no PR tested it.

TWO CANDIDATE CAUSES, not yet separated: (1) code regression in the 29 commits 619f02cf..ca31e9ae (LCLI-771 init TTY gate, LCLI-740/762 cache clear, LCLI-765 agents --check, LCLI-768 CI hardening); .bun-version is unchanged across the range. (2) The runner image changed: green run used macos-26-arm64 image 20261013.0424.1, red runs use 20261026.0455.2; same OS 26.6.2 (25G83) and same bun pin. Deciding experiment (leader-directed): workflow_dispatch of ci.yml on the OLD good SHA 619f02cf (branch diag/LCLI-760-macos-619f02cf, run 41170924075): hangs there => image; green => bisect 619f02cf..ca31e9ae with dispatches.

Not a gate for the paired 0.14.2 release decision on its own, but the runbook tags only a commit whose main CI matrix is green, so LCLI-775's metadata PR waits on this. LCLI-760 status is deliberately untouched.
implementationNotes: RESULT 2026-10-31T05:08Z: ci.yml workflow_dispatch on the OLD good SHA 619f02cf (branch diag/LCLI-760-macos-619f02cf, run 41170924075, macOS job 124448511855) FAILED the same way: both passes silent 120s, "attempt 2 ALSO failed after the hang retry". Runner image on that dispatch: macos-26-arm64 Version 20261026.0455.2 (green 619f02cf ran on 20261013.0424.1). Same OS 26.6.2, same bun 1.3.14. Conclusion: the hang follows the runner image, not the 619f02cf..ca31e9ae range; no bisect of our commits needed. Open: read the runner-images notes 20261013 to 20261026, leader decides the fix brief.

FIX (branch fix/LCLI-776-macos-runner-pin): ci.yml matrix and its Test-arm label and release.yml darwin-arm64 build leg move macos-latest -> macos-15 (image macos-15-arm64 20261028.0489.1). Evidence read by me 2026-10-31: Runner Image groups: green run 39889231736 job 120204702064 macos-26-arm64 20261013.0424.1; red 41165975631 job 124438724067 and 41170924075 job 124448511855 both macos-26-arm64 20261026.0455.2. Pin dispatches on branch: macOS leg green 41172122832 (a19297f5), 41174421793, 41174427691, 41174433292 (ff38a53d); ONE 20m job-timeout cancel 41172753074 (ff38a53d, log blob gone, cannot say silent wedge vs slow) so macos-15 is 4 of 5, not 5 of 5: DEC-236 background flake not eliminated. Control: old SHA 619f02cf with the same pin (branch diag/LCLI-776-pin-619f02cf, run 41172150510) completed its macOS Test step in about 7 min (macos-latest on that SHA hung); its only reds were the 2 ci-workflow test label assertions that old tree never updated. release.yml publish=false dispatch 41172738034 on ff38a53d: success, darwin-arm64 qualification and probe legs on macos-15-arm64 20261028.0489.1; darwin-x64 stays macos-15-intel (different image, untouched). COVERAGE LOST: macOS 26 (macos-latest) no longer exercised by CI or the release arm64 build; macOS 15 only. RETURN CONDITION: restore macos-latest (ci.yml matrix + Test arm + release.yml runner + the two test pins) once a ci.yml workflow_dispatch on macos-latest completes its macOS leg green on a runner image newer than 20261026.0455.2, repeated at least 3 times; delete diag/LCLI-760-macos-619f02cf and diag/LCLI-776-pin-619f02cf then.

EVIDENCE 2026-10-31 (lore-cli worker; all read from job logs, check-run annotations and git by me). TALLIES, ci.yml macOS leg. macos-26 before 10-26 (image macos-26-arm64): 14 jobs read, 0 log 404: 9 green-first-try, 5 job-limit cancels (39873358281, 39857558436, 39433868424, 39360965506, 37849280452), all 5 on SHAs whose ci.yml lacks the silence guard (LCLI-760 / #662, merged to dev 2026-10-23T02:08:32Z as b8655b7e); only 2 of the 14 carried the guard (39889231736, 39883131395), both green-first-try; so the pre-regression wedge rate is 5 of 12 unguarded (42%), cause of those cancels not shown. macos-26 image 20261026.0455.2: 41165975631 and 41170924075 read by me, both double-wedge (predecessor handoff also lists a rerun and main-push 41169408076 red, not re-read). macos-15 (macos-15-arm64 20261028.0489.1), 8 dispatches: 4 green-first-try (41172122832, 41174421793, 41174427691, 41174433292), 1 job-limit cancel (41172753074, log gone), 3 double-wedge (41175302106, 41175781757, 41175793397). macos-14 (macos-14-arm64 20260831.0302.1, branch diag/LCLI-776-macos-14 e8e00597), 3 dispatches 41175803187, 41175809532, 41175817202: 0 wedge, 0 green, all fail 2 tests in test/lcli630-release-window-guard.test.ts:213 (expect(r.code).toBe(0), Expected 0 Received 1; stderr not shown, not diagnosed): 1800 is accepted... and 999999999 is accepted.... WEDGE POSITION, last COMPLETED test before the 120s silence (the running test is not shown: bun --isolate prints no test-start lines); passes counted within the attempt. macos-26: 41165975631 A1 486 runCheck exit codes > nonexistent bundle root among several (LORE-225 AC#3); A2 542 runCheck status+managed-block drift (LORE-27) > a later concepts malformed markers; 41170924075 A1 1943 shell-guard accepts the safe forms > allow marker; A2 1487 Constitution lore check fails a malformed field > last_amended earlier than ratified. macos-15: 41175302106 A1 1516 Constitution markdown forms finding 6 (20,000 nested blockquotes); A2 2085 AC2 only lores built-in Constitution auto-pinned > dedupe; 41175781757 A1 1514 Constitution markdown forms finding 5; A2 520 runCheck drift > empty tasks list with stale final-task row; 41175793397 A1 513 runCheck drift > fully reconciled doc; A2 512 reconcileDriftFindings newTaskStatus null > stale zero-task block. No test repeats; attempt 2 never stalls where attempt 1 did; all on-hang samples: main thread kevent64 ~100% CPU, other threads __ulock_wait2 or __psynch_cvwait, bun frame offsets identical on both images (same bun build), unsymbolicated. READING: no single test is the common factor; the image diagnosis is weakened (0.36^3 is about 4.7% for 3 reds, not overturned) by the unguarded 42% baseline. OPEN: opum-doc A/B (A land macos-15 pin and re-dispatch wedge-class failures to reach the cut green macOS run; B hold until a label runs green without re-dispatch, starting with the 2 macos-14 LCLI-630 failures and a bun bisect). Branches kept: diag/LCLI-760-macos-619f02cf, diag/LCLI-776-pin-619f02cf, diag/LCLI-776-macos-14.

REVIEW VERDICT, as relayed by the leader, 2026-10-31. Verbatim except: markdown backticks were dropped for shell safety, and the two lines starting with "->" are the worker's pointers, not the reviewer's. Reviewer unit lore-cli-review-776, model claude-opus-5-5 read from its transcript (spawn-model verify MATCH, pid 70637, transcript 9ad28d75-4da6-4b49-8ae1-68d4c22c572a), worktree /Volumes/external/repos/lore-cli/.claude/worktrees/review-700-b8da22c. VERDICT: APPROVE, opum-ai/lore-cli#700, head b8da22cd

The change does what the ruling says it should. This approval is limited to that. It does not mean the wedge is fixed: the PR's own LCLI-776 note records 3 double-wedges in 8 macos-15 dispatches, and that question is still the open A/B with opum-doc.

FINDINGS (none blocking)

1. Non-blocking, test/ci-workflow.test.ts:81 and :181. This gap existed before the PR and still exists. Nothing checks that the matrix's macOS label and the Test arm's label are the same string. Each test hard-codes its own copy.
   - Failure scenario: someone later moves the matrix and line 81 to another label but leaves ci.yml:336 alone. Both tests stay green. The macOS leg then falls through to the bare else arm at ci.yml:404-405 (bun test --isolate --timeout=10000), with no silence guard and no sample, and goes back to dying at the 20-minute job cancel.
   - Today the two labels match exactly. A good follow-up would be to derive the arm needle from the matrix value in the test.
   -> filed as LCLI-779.

2. Non-blocking, scripts/run-hang-guarded.mjs:7. The header comment still says "bun test --isolate on macos-latest wedges". That is stale prose. The ruling keeps this file outside the PR's scope, so this is for information only. -> folds into the LCLI-776 work.

3. Non-blocking. The check job's rendered name changes from "lint · typecheck · test (macos-latest)" to "lint · typecheck · test (macos-15)". It can't be a required dev context: the matrix never includes macOS on pull_request, so it couldn't report on any PR. I couldn't read ruleset 22838594 live (no shell); that conclusion is reasoned from the workflow structure, not measured. Anything that looks up the main-push macOS job by its exact name, such as the macOS check at promotion time, needs the new name.

THE CHECKS

1. Completeness: clean. In ci.yml, every label literal under .github/ that the macOS legs depend on now says macos-15:
   - ci.yml:121 has two labels: macos-15-intel in the narrow mode (unchanged) and macos-15.
   - ci.yml:266 is the macos-15-intel arm (unchanged).
   - ci.yml:336 is == "macos-15".
   - runs-on (:122) is ${{ matrix.os }}.
   - The only other OS condition is runner.os == 'Linux' (:149). setup-bun's cache key uses runner.os/runner.arch, which doesn't depend on the label.
   - There are no include/exclude keys and no if: that compares against a label.
   - A repo-wide grep for "macos-latest" outside .quest finds only dated history in CLAUDE.md:179 and docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md:430 and :507, plus finding 2's comment. None of it is code.

2. The guarded arm runs on macOS: confirmed. The Test step (ci.yml:217-406) is an if/elif chain on "${{ matrix.os }}".
   - The right-hand side "macos-15" is quoted, so bash compares it literally, not as a glob.
   - So the earlier "macos-15-intel" arm (:266) can't capture the macos-15 leg, and the macos-15 arm can't capture the intel leg.
   - The macos-15 leg lands at :336, which runs node scripts/run-hang-guarded.mjs --silence-seconds 120 --timeout-seconds 660 -- bun test ... at :368, and again for the retry at :396.

3. release.yml: clean.
   - Read in the worktree with -o greps on line 80. The six runners in order are macos-15, macos-15-intel, ubuntu-24.04-arm, ubuntu-24.04, windows-11-arm, windows-latest.
   - The darwin-arm64 entry carries "runner":"macos-15" with "os":"darwin","cpu":"arm64".
   - darwin-x64 is still macos-15-intel.
   - The matrix is used through runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }} at :598 and :1036. Nothing compares runner values anywhere.
   - I cleared the publish job's needs and every publish gate from the diff, not by reading them. The diff has one release.yml hunk with a single -/+ pair, the line-80 matrix string, and the only token that differs is that runner value. The 5-file scope of the diff is your claim. I can't run git, so I haven't verified it independently.

4. Tests: nothing got weaker.
   - ci-workflow.test.ts:81 still matches the whole JSON array literal.
   - :181's needle '== "macos-15"' keeps its closing quote, so indexOf can't land on the earlier == "macos-15-intel" arm. Without the quote it would, and because that slice would still contain both guarded invocations, the test would pass while pointing at the wrong arm. That is the one way this edit could have quietly weakened the test, and it doesn't. All of :186-208 is unchanged.
   - ladybug-package-qualification.test.ts:294 is still an exact toEqual over all six entries, with darwin-x64 still macos-15-intel at :295.

5. .quest/tasks/LCLI-776.json is a tracker note only. I compared it by eye on the one-line diff:
   - Unchanged: id, title, status "To Do", description, priority, type, labels, references, createdAt, and the first implementationNote.
   - Changed: two implementationNotes appended (FIX and EVIDENCE), and updatedAt bumped.

6. DEC-182 path classes beyond the label: none. No permissions, triggers, action pins, secrets, env, timeouts, needs, or publish gating are touched. timeout-minutes 20 and permissions: contents: read in ci.yml are unchanged in the lines I read.

RULING 2026-10-31 (opum-doc, recorded on ODOC-556, relayed verbatim by the leader): A with a cap. Supersedes the image-regression premise of the 05:16:06Z ruling. Land the macos-15 pin (lore-cli#700, landed as 4f08a768) as a mitigation. Gate: the 0.14.2 cut needs a green full-suite macOS run at the cut SHA; re-dispatch only wedge-class failures (SILENT on both attempts, or the job limit), never an assertion failure; cap 3 dispatches per SHA, if none is green stop and bring it back to opum-doc; report every dispatch at the cut SHA, green and red. release.yml: publish needs [setup, version-parity, release-window, breaking-bump, package, release-gate-probe, provenance-pre], so a hung darwin-arm64 leg stops the release before any npm publish; same rule and cap apply to the publish:false rehearsal; on the publish:true run, re-run a wedge before publish once, otherwise bring it back. This task is retitled to the bun runtime wedge (bun bisect, symbolicated sample) and the return to macos-latest. The 2 LCLI-630 failures on macos-14 are LCLI-778 (not blocking 0.14.2). Review finding 1 is LCLI-779. Review finding 2: scripts/run-hang-guarded.mjs:7 still says macos-latest, fix with this task. Review finding 3: the main-push macOS job is now named lint · typecheck · test (macos-15); promotion-time checks must look it up by that name.
